lines: Casey Morgan
+1 (555) 010-7731 | casey.morgan@example.com | example.com/portfolio/cmorgan
EDUCATION
Lakeshore University | B.A. in Cognitive Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2015 - May 2019
EXPERIENCE
Harborview Surf School | Surf Instructor | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Taught weekend group lessons to beginners aged 8 to 60, keeping each class to one instructor for every six students.
- Ran the rental desk's morning equipment checks and logged board and wetsuit repairs for the shop owner.
Northwind Health | UX Research Associate | Metro City, USA | Jul 2019 - Feb 2022
- Raised the patient app's Net Promoter Score from 6.1 to 8.4, calculated as the average 0-10 recommendation rating across 2,000 monthly survey responses.
- Interviewed 40 patients about appointment reminders; the findings led to a two-way text reminder that cut missed appointments from 14% to 9%.
- Writes the screener and consent templates for all patient studies, cutting study setup time from two weeks to three days.
- Tested the telehealth waiting-room screens with 16 older patients; the revised layout cut support calls about joining a video visit by 30%.
Pinegrove Financial | Senior UX Researcher | Metro City, USA | Mar 2022 - Jun 2025
- Led research on the mobile onboarding flow, testing three prototypes with 24 new customers; the shipped design raised completed sign-ups from 41% to 58% in the quarter after launch.
- Improved dispute-form completion by 40% by splitting the form into three short steps with saved progress.
- Ran 18 moderated usability sessions a quarter from a recruiting panel of 400 customers, so every major release was tested with real account holders before launch.

- Synthesizing 60 interviews, 400 survey responses and 18 months of support tickets through affinity mapping, journey mapping and a tagged clip library, cut repeat support calls about statements by 23%.
- Raised the onboarding flow's System Usability Scale score from 68 to 104 across two rounds of moderated testing with 20 customers.
- Trained 12 product managers to run their own unmoderated tests with a shared script template, which doubled the number of tests run each quarter.
PROJECTS
Accessible Transit Map | Independent Project | Figma | Sep 2024 - Present
- Redesigned a city transit map for screen-reader and low-vision riders, and tested it with 12 participants on timed route-finding tasks.
- Measured the redesign with timed tasks: median route-finding time fell from 95 to 62 seconds and errors from 11 to 3 across the 12 sessions.
- Raised task success by 20% across 12 participants, from 65% to 85%, with audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
Community Clinic Booking Redesign | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Figma | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Conducted user interviews and created wireframes for a free clinic's online booking flow.
- Ten clinic patients were recruited and two rounds of hallway testing were run, and the six issues that stopped first-time users were fixed.
- Wrote the clinic's volunteer handbook for maintaining the booking pages, which two later volunteer teams used to add Spanish-language booking.
SKILLS
Tools: Figma, screen-reader testing (VoiceOver, NVDA)
Methods: moderated and unmoderated usability testing, interviews, surveys, A/B testing

items.says: Check that the portfolio URL works and leads directly to relevant research case studies.
items.because: A reviewer should be able to inspect your methods and decisions quickly.

items.says: Consider moving education below experience and projects.
items.because: Your work is now the stronger qualification for experienced UX research roles.

items.says: Put Pinegrove before Northwind, then Harborview.
items.because: The current order interrupts reverse chronology and makes your most relevant recent role harder to find.

items.says: Make the teaching bullet’s relevance to UX research clearer.
items.because: The instructor-to-student ratio explains the setting but does not show what you accomplished.

items.says: Consider removing the equipment-check bullet when space is tight.
items.because: It is less relevant to the roles your other experience suggests you are targeting.

items.says: An average 0–10 recommendation rating is not Net Promoter Score.
items.because: Calling it NPS will undermine confidence in the rest of your metrics.

items.says: Clarify your contribution to the patient-app score increase.
items.because: The bullet implies sole ownership.

items.says: Clarify how the interviews informed the two-way text feature.
items.because: It would make the link between the research and outcome more credible.

items.says: Explain how the missed-appointment rates were measured.
items.because: It would make the reported outcome more credible.

items.says: “Writes” uses the wrong tense.
items.because: The role ended in 2022.

items.says: Specify whether you created or maintained the templates.
items.because: Your contribution is unclear.

items.says: Explain how the 30% reduction was established and over what period.
items.because: This would distinguish a measured outcome from an estimate.

items.says: Clarify whether 41% to 58% is the overall sign-up completion rate.
items.because: The meaning of the change is unclear.

items.says: Clarify what part of the onboarding work you owned.
items.because: Research, design, and the shipped outcome are compressed together.

items.says: Specify whether 40% is a relative increase or a 40-percentage-point increase.
Clarify your role in the form change.
items.because: The design decision is attributed to you by implication alone.

items.says: Specify whether 18 sessions per quarter was typical or consistent throughout the role.
Reconsider “every major release” unless you can substantiate it.
items.because: It is an absolute claim.

items.says: Fix the “Synthesizing … cut” sentence structure.
items.because: It makes the actor and action unclear.

items.says: Separate what you did with the evidence from the resulting product change.
Substantiate the 23% reduction in repeat support calls.
A System Usability Scale score of 104 is invalid.
items.because: The scale runs from 0 to 100.

items.says: Give the before-and-after test counts or timeframe behind “doubled.”
items.because: The scale of the increase is unclear.

items.says: Clarify what was tested with screen-reader users versus low-vision users.
items.because: The distinction matters for accessibility credibility.

items.says: Clarify whether the Figma prototype supported the described screen-reader tasks.
items.because: The distinction matters for accessibility credibility.

items.says: Specify what the error counts represent.
items.because: “11 to 3 across the 12 sessions” is ambiguous.

items.says: Explain how the before-and-after tests were run.
items.because: The reported comparison is ambiguous.

items.says: Clarify the denominator behind 65% and 85% with 12 participants.
items.because: The percentages need a clear task-level basis.

items.says: Consider combining this result with the preceding bullet or prioritizing the most informative measures.
items.because: The results overlap.

items.says: Add what the interviews revealed or what decision they drove.
items.because: The bullet lists activities without showing their value.

items.says: Clarify whether all ten patients participated in both testing rounds.
Distinguish issues identified from issues fixed.
Make your role in the testing and fixes clear.
items.because: The passive construction obscures your role on a three-person team.

items.says: Make your contribution to the later Spanish-language work precise.
items.because: You could appear to claim that you implemented it.

items.says: List only tools you can discuss confidently.
Show in the portfolio how you used VoiceOver and NVDA if accessibility testing is a strength.
Keep A/B testing only if you can point to experience running or analyzing a test.
items.because: That experience is not evident in the bullets.

items.says: Align the methods list with what you can substantiate in your experience and projects.
